subject: Proposed hosted commit uptick, smoothing & throttle plan (Q4 renewal)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@cartloop.com>, Evan Cho <evan.cho@cartloop.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed hosted commit uptick, smoothing & throttle plan (Q4 renewal)

Hi Maya / Evan —

Thanks for the time last week. As we discussed, CartLoop's usage profile has shifted more toward long-running chat sessions and batched embeddings during peak hours. To avoid surprise throttles and give you predictable unit economics, we're proposing a modest uptick to the hosted monthly commit and a smoothing plan that pairs a burst buffer with a soft-throttle threshold. Summary of the proposal: 

- Commit increase: 30% higher monthly token commit (applies to hosted API plan line item)
- Burst pocket: additional 20% monthly burst pool for seasonal spikes (billed at current committed rate)
- Soft-throttle: automatic throttling begins if sustained 10% over the new commit for 72 hours; hard throttle still requires manual ops escalation
- Rate bands: current per-1M token rates will be reduced by 6% at the new commit tier vs today
- Term: 12 months with quarterly business reviews

I've attached a draft amendment and a short throughput plan that maps expected traffic windows against the burst pocket. Key asks for you: confirm 30% feels reasonable as a target commit, and whether procurement needs a cap on any single monthly invoice for budget control.

If that works, I can send a DocuSign-ready amendment and a HubSpot update. Would you be available Wednesday 11/3 for a 30-min ops alignment to walk the burst/soft-throttle mechanics?

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: CartLoop_Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf, throughput-plan.pdf
From: Maya Singh <maya@cartloop.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cho <evan.cho@cartloop.com>, procurement@cartloop.com
Date: 2027-10-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed hosted commit uptick, smoothing & throttle plan (Q4 renewal)

Ben —

Thanks for this, and for the clear summary. A few quick questions from our side before we lock anything in: 

1) Can you confirm the effective unit price per 1M tokens at the proposed commit (post 6% reduction)? We need that line item for FinOps.
2) For the burst pocket: can unused burst credits roll into the next month or do they expire?
3) On the soft-throttle: will there be a notification alert to our SREs and a separate approval gate before hard throttles are applied? We want an ops playbook to accompany the thresholds.
4) Procurement: we prefer a soft cap option (e.g., a monthly invoice cap) — can you propose a mechanism (credits, pre-pay, or alert-only)?

We like the 12-month term but want the QBR cadence to include a quality/regression check on outputs after quantization or model swaps. Evan, can your team join the ops call if we proceed?

Maya
Head of Product, CartLoop
maya@cartloop.com

Subject: Fwd: Proposed hosted commit uptick, smoothing & throttle plan (Q4 renewal)

FW: Maya's questions from CartLoop — need ops/finance input so we can respond with numbers and DocuSign.

Internal note: procurement is asking for a monthly cap option and they want the burst credits behavior clarified (rollover vs expire). Also they asked for an ops playbook and notifications tied to soft-throttle.

Karthik — can you confirm the discounted unit price at the proposed commit + burst handling? Laura — can you propose wording for a soft cap invoice mechanism (pre-pay / escrow / spend-alert threshold) we can offer as an optional add-on?

Thanks —
Ben
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-30T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed hosted commit uptick, smoothing & throttle plan (Q4 renewal)

Ben / Laura —

Quick feasibility and numbers from infra/finance: 

- Effective rate: at the proposed 30% commit bump and the 6% discount the blended hosted API rate would be $24.60 per 1M tokens (current committed rate: $28.00 per 1M for comparison). This assumes the same model family and no additional quantization changes.
- Burst pocket behavior: burst credits expire at month-end (cannot roll forward). Reason: burst pool is priced as capacity cushion and treating as roll-over creates accounting and capacity forecasting complexity. We can offer a 1-month grace where up to 10% unused burst is eligible for conversion to a one-time credit if you sign within 14 days, but that's an unusual exception and must be in the amendment.
- Soft-throttle notifications: we can wire automatic alerts to CartLoop SRE Slack and send an email to the ops alias when soft-throttle is triggered. Hard throttle requires a manual ops approval by Redwood with a 30-min SLA to respond under the Dedicated/Reserved contracts; for hosted we can commit to a 60-min response SLA for manual hard-throttle actions.
- Invoice cap option: finance suggests two paths — (A) pre-pay buffer (you top up a pre-pay wallet that won't be invoiced beyond the cap until wallet is depleted), or (B) alert-only cap where invoices can exceed the cap but will trigger a curated approval workflow and a fixed temporary credit if exceeded by less than 15% in any month. Option A has simpler controls but affects cash flow; Option B is easier operationally.

I've attached an updated throughput-plan that maps spike windows to the burst pocket. I'm OK to move this to a DocuSign amendment once Ben confirms preferred invoice cap mechanism.

Karthik
Head of Infra Economics, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Date: 2027-11-05T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed hosted commit uptick, smoothing & throttle plan (Q4 renewal)

Maya / Evan —

Thanks for the questions; Karthik and Laura are copied with the definitive answers. TL;DR on the actionable items we've agreed to move forward with: 

- Commit bump: 30% increase starting at the renewal effective date (month start following signature)
- Pricing: blended rate will be $24.60 / 1M tokens at the new commit tier (documented in the amendment)
- Burst credits: expire at month-end. We added a one-time conversion clause (up to 10% eligible) if you sign within 14 days of proposal — we'll put the exact language in the amendment.
- Soft-throttle & notifications: Redwood will push alerts to CartLoop SRE Slack + ops email; hard throttle will require manual sign-off with the 60-min response SLA documented in the amendment.
- Invoice cap option: recommending Option A (pre-pay buffer) for predictability; Laura, please find the suggested invoicing clause below (short): 

  "Customer may elect a pre-pay buffer up to an agreed monthly cap. Charges beyond the pre-pay buffer will be invoiced per the agreement. Redwood will not auto-increase committed capacity without written approval from Customer. Pre-pay amounts are refundable upon early termination per the contract schedule."

Next steps: I'll upload the final amendment to DocuSign (link below) with the pre-pay clause included as an optional addendum. I scheduled a 30-min call with your ops and SRE team for 11/3 at 10:30 PT to validate alert channels — if that time doesn't work we can move it.

DocuSign: https://dsc.docusign.com/CartLoop_Amendment_2027
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-000321
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bCartLoopPlan

If procurement wants to review the final amendment before routing to signature, happy to CC them on the DocuSign packet.

Best —
Ben Carter
